# Brief 036: typedef rendering delivered — the proof stands; two decisions

This morning you found yesterday's run cost too much for what it
built: 136 minutes of agent time, 70 in review cycles, 20 screen
rounds on 8 artifacts. You converged on one fix first, typedef
rendering, made it a request, and bet on it today ("Bet"). The proof had to be the bet's own decision record, made and
checked from one standard, in the same session that built the
standard. Did it work, and what now? It worked: the
initiative's measure — artifact types whose maker and checker work
from one standard — moved from 0 to 1 of 22. Confirm the approvals
taken on your direction (Ask 1) and say whether the other 21 types
get framed for your second bet (Ask 2).

**What was built.** A typedef is the definition of an artifact type —
what a decision record or a feature must contain. Until today a type's
standard lived in three hand-written documents: the typedef, a
guideline (the writing rules its maker reads), and a fitness set (the
test scenarios its checker scores against). Now the typedef alone is
hand-edited; it carries the rules and the scenarios as sections. A
compiler, the script `compile_typedef.py`, produces both from it and

hash, tying a produced document to the exact typedef it came from. A
rendering process, `typedef-rendering`, checks that every produced
document is current and re-produces any that is not; its first run
found the one converted type current. No check changed: each reads
the path it always read.

**The proof.** The PO role, the lead shop's product owner, made the
decision record for this bet from the produced guideline. Before
submitting, the author ran the produced fitness set's five scenarios
on the draft: five of five. The check then screened the record from
the produced fitness set — three rounds by a fresh-context judge, no
confident finding (a defect the judge is sure of) — and the judge's

**What gates and what defaults.** Ask 1 confirms decisions already
taken; on silence it stands. Ask 2 gates work: nothing is drafted until

**Ask 1 — confirm the approvals taken on your direction.** Three
things were approved on "Get this started" with you absent. The
`typedef-rendering` process, approved at v4 after three screen rounds.
Four typedef amendments, made by the solutions architect role (the
shop's tool maintainer): the artifact-typedef typedef (v3) admits the
two new sections and names the guideline and fitness set as produced
documents; the quality-guideline typedef (v5) and the fitness-set
typedef (v3) each admit a produced document marked as generated, naming its
source and digest, and carrying no version or history of its own; the
product-decision-record typedef (v7) folds in its guideline (v2) and
fitness set (v3), whose own histories end there. The compiler, with a

Evidence, run before this delivery from the repository root: the
compiler's check on the converted type reports no difference; the
typedef's digest recomputes to `d2e74320dabb`; the lint — the script

compiler's check and the process's screen carry them. Confirmation
binds the definitions at these versions. Recommendation: confirm.
*Default:* stands.

**Ask 2 — authorize the batch to be framed for your second bet.**
Shall the PO role draft the batch of the other 21 types as this
initiative's second feature, for your bet through the initiative check — the process that
screens an initiative and ends in your go or no-go? Recommendation:
yes, now. Evidence: the initiative's Appetite (the time you bet) names
the batch as a second bet sized after the proof, and the proof is in;
12 of the 22 typedefs have no guideline or fitness set today, so the
batch must decide what those produce — the first of four open
questions in the ADR, the architecture decision record behind this
design; and the ADR rates the decision reversible at low cost while
one type is converted and hard after the batch, so this is the last
cheap point to stop. *Default:* a note in the initiative; no work.

**What this run cost, measured.** 16 screen rounds on 6 artifacts,

content.text:
judge_stamp: claude-fable-5-1 / cold-read (stakeholder-presentation)
verdict: findings

stumbles (in reading order):
- "and bet on it today ("Bet")": the parenthetical dangles — it looks like a citation to a section I have not seen; I could not tell what it points to.
- "The proof had to be the bet's own decision record, made and checked from one standard, in the same session that built the standard": "one standard" arrives before the next paragraph explains that three documents collapse into one; I had to read on and come back.
- "No check changed: each reads the path it always read": "each" has no antecedent — which checks? I inferred "the checks that read the guideline and fitness set" but the sentence does not say so.
- "three rounds by a fresh-context judge, no confident finding": the proof is never stated to have passed. Later I learn three rounds is "the cap" and that wobbly findings pushed 5 of 6 artifacts there. So did the decision record pass, or run out of rounds? "The proof stands" in the title rests on an outcome the body does not name.
- "Three things were approved on "Get this started" with you absent": I am asked to take a two-word quote as my own standing direction covering four typedef versions, a process at v4, and a compiler. The scope of what those words authorized is not stated.
- "the artifact-typedef typedef (v3)": readable on a second pass (the typedef for typedefs), but it stopped me. Also "guideline" in paragraph two becomes "quality-guideline typedef" here — I was unsure whether that is the same thing.
- "is one of 22 the runtime lists": 22 here is skills; 22 earlier was artifact types. Same number, different populations, no signal that they differ. I wondered whether the measure "1 of 22" was counting skills.
- "two of the feature's seven scenarios ... were not demonstrated by a run this session; the compiler's check and the process's screen carry them": disclosed, but not marked as an accepted tradeoff, and the title says "delivered" and the measure "moved from 0 to 1". Under the shop's own delivery rule (checks passing do not count as done), I cannot tell whether confirming Ask 1 also means accepting the measure as met with two scenarios undemonstrated.
- "Recommendation: confirm. *Default:* stands.": no alternative is named. If I do not confirm, do the versions roll back? Is anything else waiting on my no? A confirm-only decision is not a decision I can weigh.
- "for your bet through the initiative check — the process that screens an initiative": Ask 2 describes a second *feature* of an existing initiative going through the *initiative* check. I could not tell whether that is the right gate or a slip.
- "the ADR rates the decision reversible at low cost while one type is converted and hard after the batch, so this is the last cheap point to stop": this evidence argues for pausing as strongly as for proceeding; the text uses it as urgency for "yes, now". The stop option is never put to me as a choice, only as a silent default.
- "That cut confident findings on the three the PO made ... to 4 across 7 rounds": "cut ... to 4" from what? No prior number is given, so the reduction is asserted, not shown.
- Opening paragraph measures cost in minutes (136, 70); the cost paragraph measures in rounds only. Not like-for-like — I cannot tell whether this run cost less time.
- "accepted for the small-change lane (...), defined by the PO, and applied as practice at once": "defined by the PO" — the lane, or the request? Ambiguous.
- "**Informational — no ask.** Six requests ... await your answer — accept or object": "no ask" immediately followed by six things awaiting my answer. That is an ask, or the sentence is wrong.
- "Step-communication and feasibility-defined to discovery ... no-tools-mid-process, banned-words-inlined, and maker-self-check to the lane": six slugs with no content; I cannot accept or object to a name.
- Deferred, first bullet: "The produced guideline and fitness set carry the typedef's version (7)" — Ask 1 said produced documents carry "no version or history of its own". Reconcilable on reflection (it is the typedef's version), but it reads as a contradiction on a single pass.
- "entered through the lead shop's operational contract, which has no artifact yet": "operational contract" appears here for the first time with no gloss.

unintroduced terms: "Bet" (the parenthetical); screen / screen round (used as a noun throughout; only "screened" hints at it); the cap (used as a known quantity before its one inline gloss); run / run review; the backlog order / "the order"; quality-guideline (vs. "guideline"); operational contract; work item; step-communication; feasibility-defined; no-tools-mid-process; banned-words-inlined; maker-self-check; single-review-cycle (partly recoverable from the quoted ruling); "Get this started" as a standing direction; the runtime; frontmatter.

asks:
1: wobbly — I could confirm the versions as listed, but I do not know whether confirming also accepts the two undemonstrated scenarios as done (not marked as an accepted tradeoff), what not-confirming would do, or whether the proof record itself passed or hit the cap.
2: wobbly — I lean yes on drafting, but the reversibility evidence reads as a reason to pause rather than go, the drafting effort is unsized after a morning spent on cost, and it is unclear whether the "12 types with nothing to produce" question is decided by the drafter or by me later.

overload: Over-full for one reading. The two asks are the right count, but Ask 1 carries a five-document version enumeration, the cost paragraph carries a second argument (self-check cut findings but not rounds) that no ask depends on, and the "Informational" paragraph is six opaque slugs plus a hidden third ask. Defer to the annex: the version list (keep "one process, four typedef amendments, one compiler — versions in annex"), the six request names, and the deferred bullets two and three.

top_three:
1. Make Ask 1 decidable: state the proof record's exit outcome (passed / passed at cap), mark the two undemonstrated scenarios explicitly as an accepted tradeoff or as outstanding against the measure, and name what a no-confirm does.
2. Fix the "Informational — no ask" paragraph: either turn the six routed requests into a real ask with one line each, or drop the "await your answer" and send them to the annex; remove the slugs from the brief either way.
3. Make the cost story like-for-like and grounded: give minutes for this run alongside last run's 136/70, give the baseline for "cut confident findings ... to 4", and in Ask 2 present "stop here" as an explicit option rather than only as the silent default, since your own reversibility evidence argues for it.
